prospect.name: Chris
prospect.location: San Diego, California, USA; on the US East Coast at his family home for the summer, returning to San Diego in September
prospect.occupation: Co-owner of a tequila company and several other drinks brands, with a distillery in Mexico and newly opened operations in Madrid. Five owners hold 90% of the company. Previously at Jägermeister for eight and a half years; fifteen years in the alcohol industry. Now works primarily in marketing rather than trade.
prospect.family_status: Single. Extended family staying at the house for the summer, including his sister and her husband. Has a dog.
prospect.training_background: Elite youth and college athlete — soccer for sixteen years, track, football, baseball, basketball, and a college scholarship for sprinting. Then no sport at all for ten years while working in alcohol sales, travelling roughly three weeks a month. Since April 2026 he has self-directed a turnaround with no coach: started cooking every meal for the first time in a decade, walking, and more recently walk-run interval sessions about four times a week using heart-rate zones. Has begun kettlebell work in the backyard with his brother-in-law's two 25 lb bells, following Trevor and other creators on social media. Down from 235 lb on 1 April to 212-214 lb at the time of the call, targeting 190-195 lb.
prospect.medical: Diagnosed narcolepsy. Currently off all medication as part of a trial agreed with his neurologist — previously on Vyvanse and Adderall, now using nicotine patches instead on the theory that nicotine displaces sleep-signalling hormones from shared receptors. Six months into that trial. Reports it prevents sleep attacks but does not restore energy, and that he cannot separate low energy from narcolepsy, diet or inactivity. His neurologist has told him exercise is one of the most useful interventions for narcolepsy. Tight hips, described as 'terrible'. Shoulders 'not awesome', attributed to disuse rather than injury; three days of severe shoulder soreness after his first kettlebell swing session. Transient anterior knee pain at slow jogging pace that resolves when he sprints. No history of injuries or tears. Blood work about eighteen months ago showed markers consistent with substantial under-eating. Alcohol consumption down roughly 99% from his trade years.

signals: A former high-level athlete who lost a decade to a hard professional season and wants that self back — 'I was in crazy shape before, you know, super athletic, and so my whole life, and then got in that alcohol industry'.
Explicitly names the loss: 'I miss doing sports' and 'not for the last 10 years'.
The hard season is specific and now over — 'my job was literally go out and party... go out till 2 a.m., party with bartenders, wake up at 8 a.m.' for eight and a half years.
Already rebuilding under his own steam, 22 lb down since April, which distinguishes him from a rescue case.
Not the_optimizer despite genuinely fitting the successful-business-owner profile: price was a hard barrier, not a quality signal, and he is 20 lb above his own target.

goals.text: Get from 213 lb down to 190-195 lb
Be comfortable with his shirt off at the beach this summer
Feel better and have more energy
Be athletic again and get back to playing sport after ten years away — 'I miss doing sports'
Build a stackable daily routine that makes him productive, because inconsistency destroys his output — 'when I'm all over the place and inconsistent, I'm very unproductive'
Reclaim free time by being more efficient at work — 'the more efficient I can get to work, the more efficient I can have more free time'
Train in 30-40 minutes rather than two hours in a gym

pains.text: Narcolepsy, currently unmedicated during a neurologist-supervised trial, leaving him unable to tell what his baseline energy even is
Ten years with no sport and no consistency, driven by three weeks of travel a month in the alcohol trade
Gained roughly 35 lb over a decade, then another 15 lb over one winter at home
Chronically under-ate for years; blood work showed markers comparable to a malnourished child
Tight hips described as terrible, plus stiff shoulders from disuse
Works too much and has almost no free time — 'I feel like I spend too much time working, and it's so inefficient'
Cash-poor despite a strong company valuation; all five owners take very low salaries to fund growth
Income from side businesses is unpredictable month to month and hard to forecast
Has moved roughly every three months for fifteen years, which has made any routine impossible

offer.payment_plan_terms: Third-party consumer financing through a processor the rep called Paiva, which he compared directly to Klarna. Application links were sent live in the Zoom chat for both tiers. On the three-month $4,000 option the prospect read back instalment options over three, six and twelve months, and the rep confirmed 'four hundred over twelve' — roughly $4,800 in total against a $4,000 cash price. The cost of credit was never stated. The rep also said an internal split would be preferable and interest-free, but did not structure one.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: 'there's guarantee on that also, that you will get to your goals and in six months, if not, Trevor will work for you for free until you hit this, hit those.'

prospect_financials.note: Budget stated as around $500. Owns 90% of a well-valued company alongside four partners but takes a deliberately low salary to fund growth — 'you can't take a valuation to the bank right now'. No meaningful savings to draw on. Irregular additional income from side businesses that he cannot forecast. Wants to consult his tax adviser before deciding.

evidence: No payment taken and no agreement reached on either tier.

Financing application links were sent live and opened, but a financing quote is not a purchase and the prospect did not accept one: 'let me think about it. give me a day and then I'll get back to you.'

The three-month instalment figure did fit — 'four hundred over twelve. Yeah, that's cool. That actually fits your budget' — but the prospect still deferred, citing the total: 'it's still a good amount for three months investment.'
Counter-evidence toward the positive: he committed to a decision within 24 hours — 'I'll think this over today and then I will have an answer for you tomorrow' — and agreed to a 9am phone call.
Counter-evidence toward the negative: he wants to speak to his tax adviser and cannot forecast the side-business income he would fund it from.
The follow-up was agreed verbally only, as a phone call rather than a booked calendar slot.
outcome.next_step: Rep to call the prospect at approximately 9am the following morning for a decision on the three-month $4,000 tier financed at roughly $400 a month over twelve months. No calendar invite was sent.

notable.note: Closest fit to the stated ICP in the whole batch — a genuine business owner who neglected his health while building the company, still athletic, already 22 lb down under his own steam — and he failed the offer on liquidity alone, which is precisely the pattern the ICP file already flags. Two things need escalating. First, he disclosed diagnosed narcolepsy and that he is currently off all medication in a self-directed nicotine trial with his neurologist, and was then walked through a loaded overhead kettlebell programme with no one asking whether that combination is safe. Second, the guarantee was stated here as 'you will get to your goals in six months, if not, Trevor will work for you for free until you hit those' — a materially different promise from the one the same rep gave on the Tom call the same day, which was a specific written commitment to add eight kilos to baseline kettlebell movements. Also of note: the three-month $4,000 tier appears again, invented for a second prospect on the same day, so this is a pattern rather than a one-off improvisation, and it is now being sold through consumer credit at a total above the cash price.

quality.notes: Better than the other calls in this batch but still unreliable. Short turns invert regularly and several of the rep's questions are attributed to the prospect, notably 'You sit a lot?', 'Are you drinking too?' and the entire exchange around 00:38:53 where the rep's isolation question and the prospect's answer are merged into one block. Connection dropped twice — the prospect went inside at 00:07:05 and was disconnected by clicking the financing link at 00:44:00 — and the instalment figures read back at 00:48:51 are garbled in transcription ('40, it was 15. 3, over 3, 8, over 6, 4, over 12'); only the rep's confirmation of 'four hundred over twelve' is legible with confidence. The prospect is identified only as 'Chris'; he is not the Chris Klevan who appears as sales manager elsewhere in this corpus.
